images.seen: South and Central Asia with Cliopatria: compiled shows many small states (Rajput, Maratha vassals) and anarchy-period grey in Iran; Durrani is a scatter of islands; a grey ring (about 318 unowned cells) surrounds the Kumul disk inside Qing land.

Xinjiang with Cliopatria, before the patch: Qing owns the whole Tarim Basin in 1757 (3,386 cells passed by the Dzungar dissolve) although the pages and the dossier's own ledger/23 put it with the Aq Taghliq Khojas until 1759.
Xinjiang from my stage after the patch: Tarim Basin unowned (Khojas) in 1757-1758, Dzungaria Qing, Kumul a vassal disk; 1759 gives the Tarim to the Qing.
South America with Cliopatria: Treaty of Madrid interior drawn as Colonial Brazil and Maranhao-Para as the dossiers say; Jesuit reducciones as Spanish vassal; fine as drawn.
Lake Baikal with Cliopatria: Baikal is unowned from the russian-empire_1757 keyframe snap (318 lake cells at Baikal, Ladoga and Onega leave Russia), as in Cliopatria; cosmetic, left.

Central Europe: Prussian occupation of Saxony, French occupation of Hanover, Swedish contest in Pomerania look right; East Prussia drawn contested with Russia although the Russian occupation begins in January 1758 (patched).
Durrani area (baseline stage): the Durrani core is city disks (Kandahar, Ghazni, Kabul, Peshawar, Herat) with unowned land between; Bikaner is a ring around a Mughal centre; left.
Baltic and Ukraine from my stage after the patch: Courland a Polish-Lithuanian vassal, the Cossack Hetmanate and Sloboda Ukraine as Russian protectorates instead of Russian direct land.

issues.what: Tarim Basin drawn Qing from 1757: the dzungar-khanate_1757 keyframe still holds the Tarim (3,388-cell snap), and the dissolve passes it to the Qing, against ledger/23 (Tarim lost to the Aq Taghliq Khojas in 1757) and qing-dynasty_1757 (without Tarim, falls 1759). Pages: Khojas rebelled in Yarkand, Qing campaign from February 1758, besieged at Yarkand until January 1759, 'The Tarim Basin was pacified in 1759.'

Duchy of Courland (a Polish-Lithuanian vassal 1569-1795) holds 4 of its 122 cells: the land is nobody's from 1740 (russian-empire/ledger/1, 1721, took 113 of them). Page: no change of the duchy's borders between 1700 and 1795.

Cossack Hetmanate holds 17 of its 411 keyframe cells; the left bank (Chernihiv, Poltava, Kyiv) is Russian direct land because russian-empire/ledger/1 (1721) took 342 cells. Page: the Hetmanate existed to 1764 on the left bank, infobox 'Protectorate of the Tsardom of Moscow and Russian Empire'. Restored as a Russian vassal.

Emirate of Harar holds 0 of its 316 cells from 1700: ledger/1 (1700 loss of 'the outer lands') carries the whole keyframe region. Page: 'Sovereign kingdom (1647-1875)'; Oromo clans annexed land gradually. Only the 142-cell Harar region is restored; the outer ring stays lost.

Prussia/Russia contest in East Prussia (145 cells) opens in 1757 and never ends in the window, drawn contested to 1759. Page: Russians not yet able to take Konigsberg in 1757; 'In January 1758, the Russians invaded East Prussia'; occupied over the winter and under Russian control until 1762. The contest is ended in December 1757 and the occupation drawn from January 1758.

greenland ledger/9 (1755: Ritenbenck, Egedesminde, Sukkertoppen) is skipped because the gazetteer lacks 'Saqqaq'. Egedesminde and Sukkertoppen added with the dossier's own 40 km disks; Ritenbenck not drawn (no place in the gazetteer).

Nawabs of Bengal dissolve into british-empire at Plassey (June 1757): 1,314 cells drawn as direct British land, but the dossiers (nawabs-of-bengal_1757, british-empire ledger/2 and /9) say a puppet Nawab under a British client tint until 16 August 1765. A patch cannot keep a dissolved state alive.

Kumul Khanate keyframe is a 120 km disk, while dzungar-khanate cuts a 220 km disk of Hami and the Qing shape also leaves it out, so a ring of about 318 cells round Hami is nobody's land from 1696 to 1930; a patch in my window would be undone by the Qing keyframe snaps of 1757 and 1759. The Dzungar page says only that 'Abdullah Tarkhan Beg of Hami also rebelled in 1696 and defected to the Qing dynasty' and gives no extent.
Seven Years' War: France/Prussia size-rule conflict of 21 cell-years on the Rhine (Prussia won). The Seven Years' War page does not say French troops occupied Prussian Rhineland land in 1757-1758.

Rajput and other small states against the Mughal Empire (Marwar 548, Jaisalmer 277, Bikaner 216, Jaipur 197, Bahawalpur 147, Mewar 74 cell-years), Hunza and Bukhara against Durrani and Dzungar: the smaller state won.
Bikaner is drawn as a ring (113 of 232 cells of its 140 km keyframe disk) round a Mughal centre of 109 cells in every year of the window; not traced to its cause or checked against a page.
Durrani Empire 1750-1751 is city disks (Kandahar, Ghazni, Kabul, Peshawar, Herat) with unowned land between; the 1752 keyframe fills it. Dossier choice, not checked against a page.

russian-empire_1757 keyframe (Cliopatria shape without lakes) drops 318 lake cells (Baikal 174, the other 144 at Ladoga, Onega and elsewhere) that Russia held to 1756; they stay unowned to 1761. Cosmetic.

Keyframe snaps and 1750 changes (Treaty of Madrid 12,285 and 7,643 cells, Durrani 1752, Maratha 1752, Zand 1748/1752/1757, Qing 1757, Konbaung 1753/1757, Spanish and Portuguese 1757) are dossier-ledger or Cliopatria-based and match the pages cited in the dossiers; not re-checked.

events/0 to events/3 restore land lost before my window (1721 for Courland and the Hetmanate, 1700 for Harar). If the p1700-p1709, p1720-p1729 or p1730-p1739 patches restore it earlier, mine are no-ops; a vassal_start for the Hetmanate in an earlier window would duplicate events/2.

The patch changes the p1760 start anchor (about 600 cells change owner: Courland 122, Hetmanate 359, Harar 142 and Greenland 11); p1760-p1769 starts from that.
The Zaporozhian Cossacks keep 46 cells of the Hetmanate keyframe region in 1750 and Russia holds 42 of them directly in 1759 (zaporozhian-cossacks keyframe 1752/1757); not touched.
